holidays.name: National Truffle Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating truffles, whether the fancy fungus kind or the chocolate kind. Fans of both can indulge in earthy shavings over pasta or rich, cocoa-dusted bonbons.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially in the United States, it grew out of food-celebration calendars. The date is a food-lover's invention rather than a government proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Truffle-hunting pigs were traditionally used to sniff out the fungi, but many regions now prefer dogs because pigs tend to eat the expensive find.

holidays.name: Star Wars Day (Day After)
holidays.description: Fans keep the party going the day after May the Fourth's neighbors with a galaxy-far-away hangover, though the real fun is the run-up to May 4th, when lightsaber duels and Jedi robes start appearing at the office.
holidays.origin: The Star Wars pun holiday on May 4th ("May the Fourth be with you") spread through fandom and was embraced by Lucasfilm and Disney. May 2 is often treated as the start of the countdown.
holidays.funFact: The phrase "May the Fourth be with you" reportedly appeared in a 1979 newspaper ad congratulating Margaret Thatcher on becoming prime minister.

holidays.name: World Tuna Day
holidays.description: A United Nations-recognized day highlighting the importance of tuna and the need to keep tuna fisheries sustainable. Expect fish facts, sushi, and some very serious sandwich discussions.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly designated May 2 as World Tuna Day in 2016 to raise awareness of sustainable tuna fishing and the species' ecological and economic value.
holidays.funFact: Some bluefin tuna can swim at speeds of up to about 43 mph and are partly warm-blooded, which helps them hunt in cold water.

holidays.name: International Harry Potter Day
holidays.description: Wizards, witches, and muggles gather to commemorate the Battle of Hogwarts, with costumes, butterbeer, and trivia contests. It's a day to dust off your wand and your house scarf.
holidays.origin: Fans chose May 2 because the Battle of Hogwarts takes place on that date in the final book's timeline, and they have commemorated it since the series ended.
holidays.funFact: The author has said she regretted killing off certain characters in that battle, and the date has since become a day of fan tributes.

holidays.name: National Play Hooky Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day encouraging people to ditch responsibilities for a little fun, such as a long lunch, a matinee, or a spontaneous nap. Bosses and teachers are not officially endorsing it.
holidays.origin: Considered an unofficial, humorous holiday that popped up on lists of quirky observances, in keeping with spring fever as the weather turns warm.
holidays.funFact: The phrase "playing hooky" dates to the 1800s in America, and its exact origin is still debated, with some linking it to the Dutch phrase "hoekje spelen," meaning to play hide-and-seek.
